title: Gideon and the Garden
premise: Casper Dunmore, once the storm-caller who broke the covenant between realms and doomed his homeland to endless winter, has hidden for ten years as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Vell. When a mute child named Gideon arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue, Casper realizes the boy is a living seed of the old garden—the covenant's heart—and that the long winter falling on both realms will finish unless someone reforges what he shattered. Pursued by the Pale Wardens and shadowed by his former mentor Sera, who believes the child must be destroyed, Casper journeys north to the ruined Garden of Amsel. In the end, Casper offers his own memories as soil for the new covenant: he survives, but forgets everything except Gideon's name, and together they plant a spring that neither realm will remember owing.
about_author: Noor Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write quiet, wintry fantasies about people who carry more history than they can hold.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Ten years after exile, Casper sells luck-knots in Vell, hiding his storm-gift beneath numb fingers and careful lies. A Warden inspection nearly exposes him. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of a life built on small concealments.

chapters.title: A Knock in First Tongue
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the year's first snow, a barefoot child appears at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom—words Casper knows from childhood rites. The boy cannot speak anything else. Emotional beat: dread blooming into reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: Gideon
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper names the silent boy Gideon and hides him from neighbors, teaching him bread and warmth instead of words. He recognizes the garden-sigil scarred on the child's palm—his own order's mark. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving where he expected burden.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera Vane, Casper's former mentor now serving the Pale Wardens, interrogates a smuggler about a 'speaking child' seen near Vell. She carries orders to erase it. Emotional beat: duty curdling into private doubt.

chapters.title: The Map Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Gideon draws the road north in spilled flour—an exact map to the ruined Garden of Amsel that Casper burned from every record. Casper understands the boy is the covenant's living seed. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Wardens raid the quarter; Casper flees with Gideon through the salt-gates, using a forbidden whisper of wind to cover their tracks—the first magic he's worked in ten years. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV (rendered impressionistically). Through the child's eyes, the world is loud and bright; Casper is 'the warm one.' Gideon grieves a garden he remembers but never saw. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place that exists only in blood-memory.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the river Marn, an old ferrywoman recognizes Casper's name and demands payment for a debt from the fall of Amsel. He pays with a memory of his sister. Emotional beat: survival's price made literal and small.

chapters.title: Sera Catches Up
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera corners them at a shrine but hesitates when Gideon speaks her dead mother's name in First Tongue. She lets them go one night ahead. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against grief.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In a village emptied by winter, survivors sing covenant-hymns they no longer understand. Gideon joins the song and the frozen well thaws. Hope spreads—but so does word of the miracle. Emotional beat: fragile communal hope.

chapters.title: Warden's Net
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera's superiors send a full company. Ordered to prove her loyalty, she leads them—while secretly misreading her own maps. Emotional beat: betrayal performed as protection.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Climbing toward Amsel, Casper relives flashbacks: his hand breaking the covenant stone, the first snow falling on green fields. Gideon anchors him when despair takes hold. Emotional beat: guilt confronted at altitude.

chapters.title: Campfire Confessions
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper tells Gideon the whole truth—he didn't break the covenant to save himself; he broke it because the realms demanded a sacrifice he refused to make. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into honesty.

chapters.title: The Pale Company
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Wardens' captain executes a village that sheltered the pair. Sera stops pretending; she kills two soldiers and defects into the storm. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Gates of Amsel
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They reach the Garden's ruins—a cathedral of frost-dead trees still faintly breathing. Gideon walks the paths like a child coming home. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by desecration.

chapters.title: Sera at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Wounded Sera arrives seeking forgiveness or death. Gideon speaks her mother's name again and heals her frostbite. Emotional beat: grace offered without conditions.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The final blizzard descends; the Wardens breach the Garden. Casper raises his first true storm in ten years to hold the gates. Emotional beat: fury reclaimed as guardianship.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Casper's POV (climax). At the broken covenant stone, Gideon begins to fade—the seed needs soil. Casper understands: memories are the only fertile ground left. He begins pouring his past into the roots. Emotional beat: willing self-erasure as the ultimate act of love.

chapters.title: What Casper Forgot
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. As the new covenant blooms—green bursting through snow—Sera holds Casper, who no longer knows his own history, only the boy's name. The Wardens retreat before something too alive to fight. Emotional beat: victory laced with mourning.

chapters.title: Spring, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The child, now rooted and whole, tends the reborn Garden while Casper learns the world anew like a second childhood. Sera stays as their shield. Emotional beat: gentle rebuilding.

chapters.title: The Name He Kept
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper cannot recall his crimes or his homeland, but each morning he wakes knowing he is loved and needed. Sera tells him stories of who he was, editing gently. Emotional beat: peace built on chosen kindness over truth.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Road
chapters.summary: Ensemble close. Travelers begin arriving at a garden that appeared from nowhere, carrying away cuttings and songs. Gideon presses a seed into Casper's palm—planting is a promise, not a memory. Emotional beat: inheritance continuing beyond what anyone can hold.
